The house

Three generations on the same corner of Cava Baja.

La Escalera opened in 1987 with six tables, one griddle and the notion that you could eat well in La Latina without ceremony. The same family is still behind the bar and the same griddle is still on the flame, though there are twelve tables now and a terrace that fills the moment the sun comes out.

The menu is written each morning after the market run: whatever the plaza brings sets the tone. Some dishes have not moved in thirty years — the cheesecake, Thursday's tripe, the ham croquette — because the regulars would not allow it.

The wine is chosen from small growers in Castilla y León, Rioja and the occasional Priorat. By the glass or by the bottle, with no hidden price list.

  • Market produce, every morning
  • Open kitchen
  • Wines from small growers
  • Our own terrace on the square

Frequently asked questions

Do I need to book?

For dinner Thursday to Saturday, yes, and a couple of days ahead. Book by WhatsApp or by calling from midday. At lunch midweek there is usually a table.

Are there vegetarian or gluten-free options?

Yes. Several blackboard dishes are vegetarian and the kitchen adapts almost anything. Tell us when you book and we will prepare it.

Can we bring children?

Of course. We have high chairs and the terrace is the easiest place for them. There is no children's menu, but we do half portions of nearly everything.

Is the terrace open all year?

March to October, with heaters on the cooler evenings. In winter we take it down and it is the bar inside.

We will be on the usual corner.
